data.name: Iliam
data.gender_notes: Iliam is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'El', meaning 'God'. In Greek mythology, Iliam was the name of Troy and the goddess of the city. In Christian tradition, Iliam is believed to represent the god of wine and is a derivative of Elia, meaning 'my god is Yahweh'. The name Iliam carries the meaning “God of wine” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Iliam usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wine and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the blessings of God and the importance of celebrating His divine presence.
data.etymology: Iliam belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of wine.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iliam total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Iliam originates from Hebrew and Greek roots, signifying 'God is my people'. It embodies a profound spiritual bond and commitment to one's faith community. Historically, names with similar meanings have been used in Christian traditions to express devotion and loyalty to God.

data.cultural_impact: Iliam holds a significant cultural impact from Greek mythology, as it was the name of Troy, the famous city renowned for its legendary warring Trojans. This name also represents the goddess of the city. Additionally, being a derivative of 'Elia', it is rooted in ancient Semitic and Hebrew customs, adopting the Greek 'I' prefix to represent the god within its moniker.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Iliam takes on a deeper spiritual significance, as it resembles the god of wine and is derived from 'El', meaning 'God'. The name embodies a devotion to God, holding the meaning 'my god is Yahweh'. Furthermore, it's a reminder of the possibility that every object, be it Iliam the city or a beverage like wine, can hold a connection to the divine realm and our spiritual outlook.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iliam is a name derived from the Hebrew word "Elia," meaning "God is my God." It symbolizes a deep connection and dependence on God, emphasizing faith and trust in His divine guidance.

historical_references.reference: Iliam was believed to be the site of the sacred grove of Apollo, the god of prophecy and music. This belief dates back to ancient Greek mythology, around 8th-5th century BC.
In Christian tradition, Iliam is mentioned as the place where St. Helena, the mother of Emperor Constantine I, discovered the True Cross. This supposed discovery took place around 326 AD.
